newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 'fully' implementing U.S. car pact--MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan 'fully' implementing U.S. car pact--MITI.

text.p: Japan is "sincerely and fully" implementing its part of a 1995 U.S.-Japan agreement on automotive trade and would like to see U.S. carmakers try harder, a Japanese trade official told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We are sincerely and fully implementing the agreement," the official said. "We hope for more efforts on the U.S. (carmaker) side."
The official was commenting on remarks by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, who said on Monday that Tokyo had fallen short in fulfilling the agreement to open its automotive market.

Barshefsky told Reuters in an interview, "There is no question that Japan has stalled on deregulation in this sector. "That is of significant concern and inexcusable. There is no question that the number of vehicle dealerships is also not adequate."
The Japanese trade official said, however, that it was "up to dealers" which carmaker to do business with and added that "in any case, we welcome further efforts from the Big Three in this regard".

The official said Japanese car exports to the United States were now half the level of five years ago because of increasing output in the U.S. by Japanese firms. He said this localisation trend would continue.

"If you look at the very, very short-term, it's a free economy and naturally there is some fluctuation of our exports to the U.S. because of strong U.S. demand or the exchange rate, but if you look at the medium- to long-term, localisation has been going on in the past and we think it will continue in the future," he said.
The two sides are expected to hold a review of the automotive pact in the autumn, but no dates have been set, he added.
